subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `capabilities.tts.voice.captionedFinalText` as the channel-plugin contract for deferring final-mode TTS text, beginning with Telegram?
rationale: This is a public plugin capability that changes when core suppresses user-visible text; tests can validate mechanics but cannot decide whether this is the supported long-term plugin API and ownership boundary.

options.title: Adopt the capability contract
options.body: Keep the generic opt-in capability, require current-head Telegram proof, and review the documentation as the supported external channel-plugin contract.

options.title: Keep Telegram behavior owner-local
options.body: Avoid a new shared plugin capability and ask for a narrower Telegram-owned implementation if maintainers do not want this behavior generalized.

options.title: Pause for API design review
options.body: Defer the PR until channel-plugin owners define the broader caption and text-settlement contract across voice-capable channels.

recommendation.title: Adopt the capability contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic opt-in capability, require current-head Telegram proof, and review the documentation as the supported external channel-plugin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline provides the only explicit human routing signal connected to the original review cycle; confidence remains low without local ownership history.
